questions.question: What does the name 'Akal Takht' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Akal' means timeless or beyond time, and 'Takht' (Persian) means throne, so Akal Takht is the 'Throne of the Timeless One', i.e. of Akal Purakh.

questions.question: Which two revered Sikhs completed the construction of the original Akal Takht platform?
options: Bhai Mani Singh Ji and Baba Deep Singh Ji
Bhai Nand Lal Ji and Bhai Daya Singh Ji
Baba Buddha Ji and Bhai Gurdas Ji
Baba Banda Singh Bahadur and Bhai Bidhi Chand Ji
questions.explanation: According to the Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Baba Buddha Ji and Bhai Gurdas Ji completed the construction of the Akal Takht for Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.

questions.question: The Jathedar of which Takht alone can summon a Sarbat Khalsa, and whose hukamnamas take precedence over those of other Takhts?
questions.explanation: Sri Akal Takht Sahib is the highest seat of Sikh temporal authority; its edicts issued in the name of the Panth are binding on Sikhs worldwide.

questions.question: The Akal Takht building was destroyed in June 1984 during which Indian Army action?
questions.explanation: The Akal Takht was destroyed in the army action of early June 1984 (Operation Blue Star); a new building was later raised through kar sewa.
questions.note: Operation name widely documented; Black Thunder (1986/88) is a later operation, used as distractor.

questions.question: What does the Persian word 'Takht' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Takht' is a Persian word meaning throne; the five Takhts are seats of Sikh religious and temporal authority.

questions.question: At which Takht did Guru Gobind Singh Ji create the Khalsa on Vaisakhi 1699?
questions.explanation: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib at Anandpur Sahib is revered as the birthplace of the Khalsa, where the Panj Pyare were initiated with Amrit.

questions.question: Which relic used to prepare Amrit in 1699 is preserved at Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib?
options: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's Miri sword
questions.explanation: Among the weapons and relics preserved at Kesgarh Sahib is the khanda with which Guru Gobind Singh Ji prepared Amrit at the creation of the Khalsa.
questions.source: Discover Sikhism: Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib

questions.question: Takht Sri Patna Sahib is in Patna, a city on the south bank of which river?
questions.explanation: Patna extends along the south bank of the Ganga. Takht Sri Harimandir Sahib there marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.

questions.question: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is located in which town?
questions.explanation: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is at Talwandi Sabo, about 28 km south-east of Bathinda in Punjab, where Guru Gobind Singh Ji stayed after the battles of Chamkaur and Muktsar.

questions.question: In which year did the SGPC formally recognise Damdama Sahib as the fifth Takht?
questions.explanation: The SGPC approved Damdama Sahib as a Takht by Resolution No. 32 dated 18 November 1966.

questions.question: Guru Gobind Singh Ji came to Talwandi Sabo (Damdama Sahib) in January 1706 after which battle?
questions.explanation: After his last battle at Khidrana (Muktsar) in late December 1705, Guru Gobind Singh Ji reached Talwandi Sabo, stayed about a year, and prepared the final recension of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji there.

questions.question: Which Takht is renowned as 'Guru ki Kashi', a seat of Sikh learning?
questions.explanation: Talwandi Sabo, seat of Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, is called Guru ki Kashi; tradition holds it would become home to scholars and copyists of Gurbani.
questions.note: Who first used the name is not asked.

questions.question: Which great martyr headed Damdama Sahib as a centre of Gurbani learning and is believed to have written copies of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji there?
questions.explanation: Baba Deep Singh Ji led the teaching of Gurbani at Damdama Sahib and was its chief ministrant; he is credited with preparing copies of the Granth.

questions.question: Takht Sri Patna Sahib marks the birthplace of which Guru?
questions.explanation: Takht Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib in Bihar marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji (1666), who spent his early childhood there.

questions.question: Which two of the five Takhts are located outside the state of Punjab?
questions.explanation: Takht Sri Patna Sahib is in Bihar and Takht Sri Hazur Sahib is at Nanded in Maharashtra; the other three Takhts are in Punjab.

questions.question: The central building of Takht Sri Patna Sahib was seriously damaged by an earthquake in which year, leading to the present building?
questions.explanation: The Bihar earthquake of 1934 seriously damaged the central building; the present structure was completed in 1957.

questions.question: On the banks of which river does Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib stand?
questions.explanation: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchal Nagar Sahib stands near the Godavari river in Nanded, Maharashtra.
questions.source: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib: History

questions.question: Guru Gobind Singh Ji gave the Nanded region a name meaning 'steadfast city', which appears in the full title of Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib. What is it?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji named Nanded 'Abchal Nagar' (steadfast city); the shrine is revered as Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchal Nagar Sahib.
questions.source: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib – History

questions.question: Which ruler built the shrine of Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib (c. 1832-1837)?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had the shrine built at the site where Guru Gobind Singh Ji left this world; construction took about five years.
questions.source: Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib: History

questions.question: Takht Sri Hazur Sahib is managed not by the SGPC but by a board constituted under a law of which state?
questions.explanation: Hazur Sahib is administered by a board under the Nanded Sikh Gurdwara Sachkhand Shri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib Act, 1956, a Maharashtra state law.
questions.source: The Tribune: SGPC on Hazur Sahib Act
questions.note: Act has been amended/proposed for replacement; question tests only that it is a Maharashtra state law, not board composition.
